title: Aggregate-reference scorecard & staged-traffic auto-rollback orchestration
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an aggregate-reference scorecard and integrate it with staged-traffic rollout orchestration so that canary, A/B, and shadow experiments are automatically gated and can trigger an automated rollback when statistically significant quality regressions are detected. Unlike single golden-set gates, this work composes multiple reference prompt banks (per-domain anchors, customer-specific anchors, and synthetic probes) into a weighted cumulative failure score with bootstrapped confidence intervals and a grace window to avoid flapping. The system will emit explainable signals (per-prompt failure reasons and per-metric contributions) to the Console and the rollout orchestrator and will be configurable per-project and per-customer.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard engine computes a weighted aggregate score across at least three reference banks (global anchor, domain anchors, customer anchors) and exposes an API for queries (score, CI, per-metric breakdown)
Canary/orchestrator integration accepts scorecard HTTP webhooks and performs automatic rollback when configurable thresholds are exceeded for N consecutive evaluation windows
Support for A/B splits and shadow traffic: scorecard consumes both mirrored responses (shadow) and sampled canary/A-B traffic, and attributes quality deltas to the new variant
Dashboard panels (Grafana/Console) show time-series of aggregate score, per-bank dives, bootstrap CI bands, and per-prompt examples for the last failing window
False positive rate <= 2% on historical backtests across three previously recorded rollouts (regression test suite included)
Runbook + PagerDuty playbook created and linked; on-call can mute auto-rollbacks for a specific rollout within the Console
design_decisions: Use bootstrapped sampling (not parametric z-tests) for CI because prompt-level outcomes are non-Gaussian and counts are small at early canary windows
Aggregate score is a weighted sum: global anchor (40%), domain anchors (30%), customer anchors (20%), synthetic probes (10%) — weights configurable per-project
Treat quality regressions and latency regressions separately; only quality regressions (score delta) participate in auto-rollback decision by default
Implement a grace window of 3 evaluation windows and require a minimum sample size before auto-rollback to reduce flapping
Expose per-customer baselines so Dedicated/Private customers can opt into tighter or looser thresholds without affecting global policies
Explainability: for each failing window return top 5 prompts with delta examples and a short natural-language explanation (from eval harness)

Synthetic injection tests: create PRs that change generation distribution and ensure score delta triggers after configured windows

notes: This approach intentionally avoids a single golden-set blocker; instead we provide a tunable, explainable multi-banked score so product teams can trade sensitivity vs stability
